rule: Payment labelled DUPLICATE_PAYMENT and sender is a business -> An earlier payment exists with same sender, beneficiary, currency and amount
interpretation: INTERPRETATION: back-office race condition re-submits the same payment
when_condition: Payment labelled DUPLICATE_PAYMENT and sender is a business
then_effect: An earlier payment exists with same sender, beneficiary, currency and amount
exceptions: C senders: different sender account (partner) and longer gap?
rejected_alternative: Exact copy of the row (rejected: timestamps differ)

rule: Payments are made in the sender country's local currency
test: full data; local currency inferred in-sample
value: 89.4% sender-local; only 4.2% use the receiver currency instead (18.9% match the receiver currency incl. same-currency pairs)
interpretation: The sender's bank debits in its home currency; FX happens later along the route

rule: Direct payments: 1 conversion if sender and receiver local currencies differ, otherwise 0
test: prediction accuracy on all Direct rows
interpretation: With only two banks, FX happens once, and only between currency areas

rule: Conversions never exceed the number of hops (participants - 1)
interpretation: Each correspondent bank can convert at most once

rule: Amounts are log-normal: ln(amount) is normal with the same spread for every pair
test: skew / excess kurtosis / sd of ln residual
interpretation: Payment sizes built from many multiplying factors are naturally log-normal

rule: Each business party (sender or receiver) multiplies the amount by e^2 = 7.4
test: ln effect within sender country, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI
interpretation: Businesses pay invoices and payroll; consumers send small personal transfers

rule: The sender's country sets the base amount; the receiver's country adds nothing
test: R² sender country vs extra R² of receiver country
interpretation: Payment size scales with the income level of the sending economy (compare with GDP per capita, cited as a reference)

rule: Sender type and receiver type are assigned independently
interpretation: Who pays and who gets paid are separate draws

rule: Timestamps follow the sender's local working day (same for B and C)
test: share 07:00-19:59 local vs UTC; V(hour, sender type)
interpretation: Payments are entered and batched in office hours

rule: Business sender accounts send more payments than consumer accounts
test: payments per (sender BIC, account) over the data window
interpretation: Companies pay many suppliers and staff

rule: CEO scams only come from business senders; romance scams only from consumer senders
test: labelled anomalies by sender type (full data)
value: CEO: B 945, C 0; romance: B 0, C 2476
interpretation: Each scam targets a specific kind of victim

rule: Handout example: consonant currency codes give 3x amounts
test: ln residual difference consonant - vowel (3x would be +1.099)
interpretation: The handout example is illustrative, not a rule in this dataset

rule: Cross-border payments are smaller than domestic ones
test: raw median ratio vs within-country ln effect
value: raw x0.62; same country and party types x1.00
interpretation: Domestic payments come from richer countries; crossing a border itself changes nothing
